note: Dates and holders are editable here. Source: unclehowell/cedwyn-infographic public/data/transfers.json (v3.6.0, 2026-11-04). Status solid = record seen; dashed = family case or record not seen.

events.title: One holding under the Bute Estate
events.reason: family research chain; earlier title under examination
events.text: The farm ground is drawn as a single holding. The Bute Estate is shown as holder on the family’s research chain; the earlier chain of title is still under forensic examination and is not asserted here.

events.title: 1877 · the land is split
events.text: Agreement between the Bute Estate and Daniel Thomas & Son: sale, or quarry lease, of the house parcel. The agreement itself is not in hand. The map now shows the split: Parcel A (north wood, house and yard, the green) goes to Daniel Thomas & Son; Parcel B (the fields east of the house) stays with Bute. The outlines of the north wood and the green are the family’s reconstruction (estimated).

sources.t: EV-0291 · NLW Bute Estate catalogue D153 (Llandough limeworks land, 1876–1912)

events.title: 1926 · Parcel B: Bute estate becomes Mountjoy Ltd
events.text: Remaining Bute property incorporated as Mountjoy Ltd.

sources.t: Glamorgan Archives DA catalogue (Bute estate history)

events.title: 1928 · last rent paid; Parcel A with the family
events.text: No deed held. On the family's case, the 1877 arrangement resulted in Parcel A passing to the Williams family when quarrying ended and the last rent was paid in 1928.

events.title: 1938 · Parcel B conveyed to Western Ground Rents
events.text: Conveyance on sale, Mountjoy / Bute to Western Ground Rents Ltd, 25 Dec 1938 (recited in later WGR deeds).

sources.t: EV-0216 · recital of the conveyance of 25 Dec 1938

events.title: 1942 · woodland at Leckwith gifted to Cardiff Corporation
events.text: Gift of about 110 acres of woodland at Leckwith, WGR to Cardiff Corporation. About 110 acres of Leckwith woodland. This is other ground, not one of the four parcels drawn on the map; it is shown because Cardiff Corporation later appears on the north wood.

sources.t: EV-0259 · Leckwith Woods, 1955 lease and boundary measure

events.title: 1955 · the possession order
events.text: Order 14 possession order, executed 4 July 1955. Parcel B is taken by Western Ground Rents under the executed order (record seen). On the family’s case the same order took the woodland and the green; that part is drawn dashed because the record has not been seen. The woodland then appears in Cardiff Corporation’s 1961 deed and the green is registered as VG41 in 1970.

sources.t: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (judgment)
EV-0034 · 1955 writ of possession and return
1955 loss dossier: the woodland (Parcel A) and the green (outside Parcel A)

events.title: 1961 · the woodland goes to Cardiff Corporation
events.text: Deed of 29 March 1961 between (1) Western Ground Rents Ltd (2) The South Western Brick & Tile Company Ltd and (3) Cardiff City Corporation, listed on the woodland title WA735527.

sources.t: EV-0040 · 29 Mar 1961 deed (WGR, South Western Brick & Tile, Cardiff City Corporation)

events.title: 1962 · the farmhouse and garden are taken
events.text: Cardiff County Court possession order of the farmhouse and garden (Judge Temple Morris QC).

sources.t: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (judgment)
EV-0041 · 1962 Cardiff County Court possession order

events.title: 1969 · WGR conveys to BP Pension Trust
events.text: Conveyance, WGR to BP Pension Trust, recited as the root of BP’s title. For the house it carried the benefit of the 1962 order. The house and fields pass to BP Pension Trust (record seen). The woodland is drawn dashed: the title history runs WGR → BP, but no 1969 deed for the woodland is held and it sits awkwardly with the 1961 deed to Cardiff Corporation. That conflict is unresolved in the archive.

sources.t: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (judgment)
EV-0043 · 1969 conveyance, WGR to BP Pension Trust
EV-0288 · 1968–69 press on the WGR takeover
Forest of Cardiff assessment (woodland title history)

events.title: 1970 · the green is registered as a village green (VG41)
events.text: Village-green registration VG41, 16 June 1970. Registration authority: Glamorgan County Council. This is a registration record, not a conveyance.

sources.t: Llandough Community Council: village green page

events.title: 1983 · BP Properties registers the house and fields
events.text: First registration of the house, title WA240304, to BP Properties Ltd (Form 1C application, 23 Feb 1983). The house is first registered (WA240304). The fields follow on the 1982 application for WA231076 (record not seen).

sources.t: Three parts of Parcel A: licence letters (31 Oct 1974), then first registration (wiki)
BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (the 1974 letters)

events.title: 1987 · Court of Appeal: BP Properties v Buckler
events.text: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler: possession of the farmhouse and garden. The appeal was limited to the farmhouse and garden. The titles of the house and the fields were merged on 2 Feb 1987, while the appeal was running. No land changed hands.

sources.t: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (judgment)
EV-0078 · 1987 title amalgamation application and plan

events.title: 1988 · possession taken; Great House Farm demolished
events.text: Possession was taken on 29 Nov 1988 under the order upheld by the Court of Appeal on 31 Jul 1987, and the farmhouse was demolished on 6 Dec 1988. The building drawn here is a plain stand-in, not a model of the real house.

sources.t: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (judgment)

events.title: 1993 · sold on to Ideal Homes for housing
events.text: Sale of the merged title (house and fields) for housing. The woodland moves to Ideal Homes on 3 Dec 1993 (record not seen); the house and fields are sold for housing in 1993–94.

sources.t: EV-0276 · press, 1994–96: Ideal Homes, Church View Close, Persimmon
Forest of Cardiff assessment (woodland title history)

events.title: 1994 · Church View Close is built
events.text: Houses are built over the farmyard and fields. The modern buildings on the map are today’s, from OpenStreetMap, so they appear together at the start of the building programme rather than house by house.

sources.t: EV-0276 · press, 1994–96: Ideal Homes, Church View Close, Persimmon

events.title: 1994 · the woodland is transferred to Forest of Cardiff
events.reason: transfer deed and plan not seen
events.text: Transfer to Forest of Cardiff under title WA735527, dated 10 Nov 1994 (the current register shows proprietor entry 25 Nov 1994).

sources.t: EV-0136 · 10 Nov 1994 transfer to Forest of Cardiff, with plan

events.title: 1995 · house sales at Church View Close
events.text: House sales at Church View Close (first buyers by January 1995). First buyers by January 1995; Persimmon buys Ideal Homes with the unsold plots in early 1996, and the last house is sold by September 1996.

sources.t: EV-0276 · press, 1994–96: Ideal Homes, Church View Close, Persimmon

events.title: 2005 · part of the woodland sold to Goldsworthy Homes
events.text: Part of the woodland sold to Goldsworthy Homes and taken out of title WA735527.

sources.t: EV-0217 · Forest of Cardiff accounts to 30 Jun 2006
EV-0139 · 2005 transfer, Forest of Cardiff to Goldsworthy Homes

events.title: Today
events.text: This is where the archive leaves the land. The solid and dashed outlines show which holders rest on records we have seen and which rest on the family’s case or on records still to be found. The loop now starts again.
